articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA, the agency that's supposed to protect everyone else's secrets, just face-planted by letting a contractor dump AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's a goddamn yard sale. Congress is rightfully losing their minds over this beautiful irony.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: The cybersecurity watchdog left the henhouse door wide open - a CISA contractor published highly privileged AWS credentials on public GitHub for any script kiddie to stumble across. Peak operational security right there.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare win for end-to-end encryption, that magical thing that turns your messages into unreadable gibberish for everyone except the person you're actually talking to. Revolutionary concept, apparently.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF drops a new guide on fighting back against the surveillance state because apparently we need step-by-step instructions to remember that mass spying is bad. The systematic human rights violations won't fix themselves.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google's API keys have a fun 23-minute zombie window after 'deletion' where they're still perfectly functional - because immediate deletion is apparently more of a suggestion than a feature. Classic cloud provider move.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Trump Mobile's website was hemorrhaging customer data to anyone who could craft an HTTP request, which is basically the digital equivalent of leaving your diary on a park bench. MAGA-level security right there.

articles.title: Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective
articles.summary: The Megalodon campaign auto-poisoned over 5,500 GitHub repos in six hours using throwaway accounts and CI/CD workflows. It's like supply chain attacks met industrial automation and had a very productive baby.

articles.title: SailPoint Announces New Integration with the Claude Compliance API to Provide Enterprise-Grade Identity Security for AI Platforms
articles.summary: Microsoft's BitLocker can apparently be bypassed with a USB key in what a security researcher calls an intentional backdoor. Because why build proper encryption when you can leave a secret key under the digital doormat?

articles.title: GitHub Confirms 3,800 Internal Repos Stolen Through Poisoned VS Code Extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP is poisoning open source code at unprecedented scale, turning GitHub into their personal malware distribution network. Supply chain attacks are having their main character moment.

articles.title: Re: Linux kernel: Dirty Frag variants — fix merged into netdev
articles.summary: GitHub got absolutely owned through a poisoned VS Code extension, losing 3,800 internal repos to TeamPCP hackers. The irony of the world's largest code repository getting pwned through malicious code is *chef's kiss* perfect.
